S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report to the relevant regulator every thermal incident involving overheating, fire, injury, or property damage within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, with a complete incident report within 10 business days. They must notify affected customers within 48 hours when an incident presents a credible safety risk to their unit or household, and promptly update those customers as material facts emerge.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: A model with a failure rate above 7% may not be newly placed on the market. For a model above 5% but no more than 7%, the manufacturer must promptly provide results to regulators and customers purchasing that model, submit a regulator-approved remediation plan, and retest after corrective changes.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: Remote emergency shut-off is required on all new units placed on the market from 24 months after adoption. Manufacturers must provide a retrofit path for installed units and complete required retrofits within 6 years of adoption, subject to safe technical feasibility; customers must receive clear instructions on availability and operation.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New units placed on the market must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption of this standard.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: When a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents involving overheating or fire per 100,000 installed units in any rolling 12-month period, the manufacturer must promptly notify the regulator and submit the relevant incident data. The manufacturer must submit and carry out a time-bound corrective-action plan under regulator oversight. A recall is mandatory if the regulator determines there is an imminent or unmitigated serious risk, or the manufacturer fails to carry out the required plan; affected customers must then be notified promptly and offered an effective remedy or safe decommissioning instructions.

document.section_notes: The S2 limit was loosened from 5% to a permanent 7% cap, which keeps Northwind's Hearth 10 (6.2%) on the market, and S5 replaced automatic recall at 8 per 100,000 with open-ended regulator-led corrective action, which protects Halcyon's Ember 8 (9.9). S1 reporting is strong (24-hour reporting for all thermal incidents), S4's 36-month suppression start sits inside the acceptable range, and S3's 24-month new-unit start and open 'subject to feasibility' retrofit escape are weaker than the answer key. The results_to_customers value is coded as numeric_rates because the text says 'results' without specifying numeric rates; this does not change any section's rating.
